class_id: a live ipos row created outside consolidation has zero field_sources rows, and stays invisible to every per-field provenance check forever
feature: any live (UPCOMING/OPEN) offering_type=IPO row whose fields were written by something other than the consolidation write path (a seed insert, a manual/legacy insert, an admin create that bypassed the pull model) and that has never subsequently been re-walked by a source
symptom: field_sources records who supplied each field's current value, written only by the consolidation path. Every existing per-field provenance check (e.g. checkSegmentHasProvenance / checkPublishedWithoutProvenance) fires when a FIELD holds a value with no field_sources row for it — but a row that never went through consolidation at all has no fields with values to be missing provenance FROM in the check's per-field sense; it just has zero field_sources rows, period. That shape reads as "nothing to check" to a per-field check, not "never checked", so the row is structurally invisible to the entire per-field provenance audit surface. It stays that way until the scraper's normal cycle happens to re-walk it — which, being a live IPO with a documented last-scrape date, never became due again because nothing marks a zero-provenance row as needing a walk sooner.
